title: Patriot missile failure at Dhahran: time-conversion precision loss after extended uptime
summary: GAO reported that on February 25, 1991 a Patriot battery at Dhahran failed to track and intercept an incoming Scud, which hit an Army barracks and killed 28 Americans. The tracking calculation became less accurate the longer the system operated; the battery had run continuously for more than 100 hours, and a modified software version reached Dhahran the day after the incident. This record is high-sensitivity and is framed around system learning, not spectacle.

type_payload.system: Patriot air-defense battery/radar/range-gate/weapons-control-computer operating in anti-Scud role

sequence_of_events.event: Patriot system was deployed in a role and operational tempo different from the original design assumptions described by GAO.
The Dhahran battery operated continuously for more than 100 hours.
Precision loss in time conversion shifted the range gate away from where the Scud would next be detected.
The system failed to track and intercept the incoming Scud.
The Scud hit an Army barracks, killing 28 Americans.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Range-gate prediction degraded due to software numeric-precision loss tied to extended uptime.
type_payload.root_cause_source_language: software problem in the system's weapons control computer
contributing_factors: System had not previously been used to defend against Scud missiles and was not expected to operate continuously for long periods.
Internal registers had limited precision for the relevant time conversion unless software compensated for the limitation.
Israeli data indicated range-gate shift after 8 hours, but corrective software distribution did not reach the Dhahran battery before the incident.
GAO notes that internal data recording was not embedded and portable recorders were not used by U.S. commanders due to concern they could cause shutdown.
latent_conditions: Operational use drifted beyond original assumptions: mobile, short-duration air-defense operation became long-duration fixed anti-missile defense.
Software updates and warnings did not close the hazard before exposure continued.
Data collection and feedback paths were limited in wartime operations.
decisions_that_mattered: Leaving the system continuously on for over 100 hours in the Dhahran context.
Not installing or receiving the modified software before the incident.
Not using portable data recorders in U.S.-controlled systems, limiting direct performance data.
recommendations_extracted: GAO report focuses on what happened and correction status; a fuller recommendations extraction remains a next action.
counterfactuals_source_grounded: Software compensation for hardware precision limitations, timely distribution of modified software, or operational reset/shutdown discipline could have reduced the specific failure pathway; each requires deeper source review before being stated as a proven prevention.

links.note: Numeric representation precision and uptime assumptions escaped their expected domain.
